def.brief:
Change worker.py, and only worker.py, so that every sentence N1-N7 below holds. test_native_prompt.py (written to this contract by the tests writer, committed) and test_hacheong.py are the protected tests: do not change either. The contract fixes the native section's text exactly, that --host has no effect on --prompt-only output, and that the claude/codex subprocess path is unchanged, so no behaviour choice should be left to you; internal shape is yours (for example how assemble is told to render the native section), provided environment_text(member, host) and assemble(member, request, domain, target=None, host=None) keep rendering exactly as N6 says for host "claude", "codex" and None, and the claude/codex adapters keep their (prompt, member, args, target) -> (answer, stream) form. The module docstring's --prompt-only usage line and any comment you touch must stay true of the new behaviour; follow the file's existing comment style. Do not touch hostcall.py, hacheong.py, README.md, skills/, members/, domains/ or any manifest; add no CLI option, host or model override, and change no sandbox.

CONTRACT (sentences N1-N7). Defect: worker.py assembles the --prompt-only prompt with the Claude subprocess environment regardless of --host, so a native subagent (a session's own subagent, e.g. a Codex spawn_agent) is told Claude tools, "Network: yes" and loopback that nothing established. Switching it to the codex rendering would be just as false (a Codex subprocess sandbox does not apply to a native subagent). --prompt-only gets one neutral native environment section instead; the normal subprocess path is unchanged. No new CLI option, no host or model override, no sandbox change.

NATIVE (the exact `# Where you run` section a --prompt-only prompt carries, heading line, blank line, then exactly these two lines):
# Where you run

You are a subagent the parent session dispatched itself (a native call); this prompt was printed by `worker.py --prompt-only`, which grants nothing. What you may read, write and run, your tools, and whether you have the network or loopback (binding a local port) come from the parent host and its configuration, not from this text. This runner starts no subprocess for you — none of its sandboxes applies — and runs none of its validators on your answer.
S

where S is this existing sentence, verbatim (it is already the last line of every current rendering):
What the work needs and this place lacks — a package, a tool, the network, a file outside `target` — is not yours to work around: stop with `status: blocked` and name it. When it is the network or loopback, list it in `lacked` (`["loopback"]`, `["network"]`), not only in prose — the runner reads `lacked`, not your sentences; nothing lacked: `lacked: []`. Do not write by hand what a tool generates (a lock file, a build output) and do not swap in another tool for the one the request names.

N1. `python3 worker.py --member M --request F --response R --prompt-only` with `--host claude`, with `--host codex`, and with no `--host` exits 0, writes no response file, starts no host session, and prints a prompt whose `# Where you run` section (from that heading up to `# Request`) is exactly NATIVE — for every shipped member (dakdol, sibi, teujip, chojja).
N2. For the same member, request and domain, the whole --prompt-only stdout is byte-identical for `--host claude`, `--host codex` and no `--host` — also when AGENT_CODEX_SANDBOX is set in the environment (e.g. `danger-full-access`) and when a project-local member's policy.json sets `can` (e.g. {"network": true, "loopback": true}) or a different `sandbox`.
N3. A --prompt-only `# Where you run` section never promises an environment: it contains none of "A Claude Code session with these tools only", "Network: yes", "Network: no", "Loopback — binding a local port", "A Codex sandbox", "`read-only`", "`workspace-write`", "no network", nor the member's policy `tools` string (e.g. "Read,Grep,Glob").
N4. Genuine unmet-capability reporting is kept in --prompt-only: its section ends with S verbatim, and the `# Answer` schema still lists `lacked` in `properties` (items enum ["network", "loopback"]) and in `required`. (Preservation: may pass before the build.)
N5. The --prompt-only prompt keeps the contracts: sections in order `# Who you are` < `# The domain: <domain>` < `# Where you run` < `# Request` < `# Answer`; the JSON object printed in `# Request` (after the line "Work only inside `target`. Do not write the response file; answer with the JSON object.") parses equal to the request file's object, including non-ASCII text and a `needs` field; the JSON after "matching this schema:\n" in `# Answer` parses equal to `worker.load_member(M)["schema"]`. A request with `"needs": ["loopback"]` under `--host codex --prompt-only` is still printed (exit 0, no response file): the native host, not this renderer, decides. (Preservation: may pass before the build.)
N6. The subprocess renderings are unchanged. With AGENT_CODEX_SANDBOX unset, `worker.environment_text(member, host)` for host "claude" and "codex", and so the `# Where you run` part of `worker.assemble(member, request, domain, target, host)`, is exactly as before: "# Where you run\n\n" + L1 + "\n" + L2 + "\n" + S, where for host "claude" L1 = "A Claude Code session with these tools only: " + <policy tools, default Read,Grep,Glob> + "." and L2 = "Network: yes. Loopback — binding a local port (a local server, `wrangler dev`, a fake S3 on 127.0.0.1): yes."; for host "codex" with sandbox `workspace-write` (dakdol, teujip, chojja) L1 = "A Codex sandbox (`workspace-write`): you can write inside `target`. By default it has no network — package installs and downloads fail — and `.git` is read-only: no commit, no `git mv`, no branch." and with sandbox `read-only` (sibi) L1 = "A Codex sandbox (`read-only`): you can read and run commands, not write, and there is no network.", and for codex L2 = "Network: no. Loopback — binding a local port (a local server, `wrangler dev`, a fake S3 on 127.0.0.1): no.". Shipped tools: dakdol and teujip "Read,Edit,Write,Glob,Grep,Bash", sibi "Read,Grep,Glob", chojja "Bash,Read". `worker.assemble(member, request, domain)` with no host still renders the claude form. (Preservation: may pass before the build.)
N7. Without --prompt-only, `worker.main()` hands the host adapter — `worker.claude` for `--host claude`, `worker.codex` for `--host codex`, each called as `(prompt, member, args, target)` and returning `(answer, stream)` — a prompt whose `# Where you run` section is that host's N6 rendering, never NATIVE. A test may replace `worker.claude` / `worker.codex` in-process with a stub that records the prompt and returns a canned answer; no model is called. (Preservation: may pass before the build.)

Out of scope: hostcall.py, hacheong.py, README.md, skills/, members/, domains/ and every manifest stay as they are; test_hacheong.py stays as it is and must keep passing (`python3 test_hacheong.py`).
